subject: physics
title: Photoelectric Effect Revisited
welcome_lead: Test Einstein's photon equation hf = φ + ½mv²_max in three classic experiments.
meta_desc: A-Level Quantum Phenomena adventure on photoelectric experimental observations.
final_note: Photoelectric results killed the wave-only theory of light for good.

concepts.def: Minimum energy to free an electron.
Determines rate of electrons, not KE.
Begins as soon as f ≥ f₀.

walkthroughs.body_html: 1) Threshold frequency exists. 2) Below f₀, no emission, even at high intensity. 3) KE_max depends on f, not intensity. 4) Emission is instantaneous.
Each photon gives all its energy to one electron. Part (φ) frees it; the rest is KE. KE_max = hf − φ.
Reverse-bias the collector until current drops to zero: eV_s = KE_max. Plotting V_s vs f gives line with gradient h/e and intercept φ/e.

mcqs.q: Increasing the intensity of incident light (f > f₀):
options: Raises KE_max
Increases current of photoelectrons
Raises threshold frequency
Has no effect
h φ
φ / h
h / φ

mcqs.q: What is the threshold frequency in the photoelectric effect?
options: Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
The frequency at which photons travel at the speed of light.
The minimum intensity of light needed to eject electrons.
The minimum frequency of light required to eject electrons from a given metal — it equals the work function divided by Planck's constant.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency not eject electrons?
options: Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
The frequency at which photons travel at the speed of light.
Each photon's energy is below the work function; many low-energy photons can't combine to eject an electron.
Enough low-frequency photons should eventually eject an electron if you wait long enough.

mcqs.q: What determines the energy of a single photon?
options: A brighter light has higher-energy photons because intensity makes each photon more energetic.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
Its frequency (E = hf) — only frequency, not intensity.
The frequency at which photons travel at the speed of light.
